chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Whoever vomits deliberately while fasting has broken his fast, and he must make up for it; if Allah wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him."
And he said: "Whoever vomits while fasting, upon him is the making up (of the fast)."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if a person vomits deliberately or involuntarily?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the chain of Harun ibn Muslim, the distinction is drawn between deliberate vomiting, which definitively breaks the fast and incurs the obligation of qada', and involuntary vomiting, which also requires qada' but is treated with divine mercy. This ruling is situated within the broader jurisprudential discussion on the validity of fasting during medical treatments, emphasizing that the intent behind the act determines the severity of the break. The Imam’s mention of Allah’s choice to punish or forgive highlights the balance between legal obligation (wajib) and divine grace in Shia fiqh.
